hero.headline: Supreme Court reinstates Republican-favored Alabama congressional map
hero.teaser: The Court's decision means Alabama's 2026 midterm elections will use a map with six Republican-leaning districts and one Democratic-leaning district.
hero.body:
The U.S. Supreme Court has allowed Alabama to use a redrawn congressional map that eliminates one of the state's two majority-Black districts, issuing a 6-3 decision that represents a significant victory for Republicans and a setback for Black voters.

The ruling permits Alabama to implement its 2023 map in the upcoming midterm elections. A lower court had previously determined that this map was intentionally drawn to discriminate against Black voters and violated the Voting Rights Act. A three-judge panel had rejected the map and ordered a special master to redraw it, which resulted in two majority-Black districts. The panel also issued an injunction preventing Alabama from using another map until after the 2030 census.

Despite these findings, the Supreme Court's majority lifted the injunction without providing any explanation for its decision. The three liberal justices dissented strongly. Justice Sonia Sotomayor wrote that the court had "unceremoniously discards the District Court's meticulously documented and supported discriminatory-intent finding" without sound basis. She noted that "the record showed that Alabama made an intentional choice to perpetuate and entrench, rather than remedy and uproot, the racial discrimination."

Under the reinstated map, Alabama will have five congressional districts represented by white Republicans and two represented by Black Democrats. Notably, the new map eliminates the seat held by Representative Shomari Figures, which stretched from Mobile through the state's Black Belt, and replaces it with a Republican district.

The Supreme Court's decision comes just days after the same court gutted Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act in a case involving Louisiana's congressional districts. Alabama quickly returned to the Supreme Court following that ruling to request removal of the injunction, which the court granted on Monday.

The decision reflects an aggressive approach by the court's conservative majority in allowing Republican-controlled states to redraw districts that reduce the influence of Black voters. In the past, the Supreme Court has generally refused to overturn election rules on the eve of elections. However, the court has now abandoned this principle in both the Louisiana case, where it issued its decision while voting was underway, and in Alabama.

Republicans in other states have moved quickly to capitalize on this development. Tennessee, Louisiana, and South Carolina have all begun efforts to implement new maps designed to boost Republican electoral chances in the upcoming elections.

The Alabama primary was originally scheduled for May 19, but Republicans passed legislation last week moving the date in anticipation of the Supreme Court's action. The new map will shape how Alabama's voters are grouped and represented in the House of Representatives for the current election cycle.

cards.headline: U.S. and Iranian forces exchange strikes as peace talks stall
cards.teaser: U.S.
cards.body:
U.S. and Iranian forces exchanged strikes Tuesday as peace talks remained stalled and tensions escalated across the Middle East. American aircraft fired on Iranian military sites over the weekend, including Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway through which roughly one-fifth of global petroleum passes.

The U.S. military characterized its response as self-defense against Iranian aggression across the region. The confrontation widened beyond direct exchanges between the two nations, raising concerns about potential broader regional conflict as diplomatic efforts showed no signs of progress.

cards.headline: US Proposes Tariffs of at Least 10% on 60 Countries Over Forced Labor
cards.teaser: The US announced plans to impose tariffs on dozens of trading partners following an investigation into forced labor practices.
cards.body:
The United States has proposed tariffs of at least 10% on goods from approximately 60 countries, citing inadequate efforts to prevent forced labor in their supply chains. The tariffs would affect major trading partners including Canada, Mexico, and the European Union, with rates ranging from 10% to 12.5% depending on the country.

The proposal stems from a US government investigation into forced labor practices in global trade. The administration views the tariffs as necessary to address what it considers insufficient action by trading partners in keeping goods made with forced labor out of international commerce.

cards.headline: Ukrainian Attack Sets Russian Weapons Plant Ablaze
cards.teaser: A weapons manufacturing facility in Russia's Tambov Oblast caught fire following a Ukrainian strike.
cards.body:
A Russian weapons manufacturing facility in Tambov Oblast caught fire following a Ukrainian strike targeting military production infrastructure deep within Russian territory. In a separate operation, Ukraine also attacked an oil terminal in St. Petersburg. Moscow Region activated emergency protocols and mobile warning systems in response to drone threats.

The attacks occurred one day after Russia launched a massive aerial assault on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities, killing at least 22 civilians and wounding 138 others. The strikes continued throughout the day as Russia escalated fighting across multiple fronts.

cards.headline: Canada Requests 16-Year Extension of North American Trade Agreement
cards.teaser: Canadian officials formally asked the US and Mexico to renew the USMCA trade pact for another 16 years.
cards.body:
Canadian Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc has formally requested a 16-year renewal of the USMCA trade deal in a letter to his counterparts in the United States and Mexico. The proposal aims to extend the North American free trade agreement that currently governs hundreds of billions of dollars in annual trade across manufacturing, agriculture, and services sectors.

The request comes amid broader trade tensions between the three nations. LeBlanc met with the U.S. Trade Representative on Tuesday to discuss the renewal proposal.

cards.headline: Seven States Sue Trump Administration Over $1 Billion Deal to Halt Offshore Wind Farm
cards.teaser: New York and six other states filed suit challenging a payment to TotalEnergies to cancel a wind farm project.
cards.body:
Seven states sued the Trump administration over a nearly $1 billion deal to halt an offshore wind farm project. The administration paid French company TotalEnergies to cancel plans to build offshore wind farms, according to reports from multiple news outlets.

New York led the lawsuit, with officials characterizing the agreement as a fabricated deal designed to block renewable energy development. The states argue the payment represents an improper use of federal funds to prevent clean energy projects from moving forward. The lawsuit seeks to block the deal and recover the funds paid to the company.

cards.headline: Trump administration drops $1.8 billion payout fund after Republican opposition
cards.teaser: The Justice Department will not proceed with a fund that faced backlash from GOP lawmakers.
cards.body:
Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche announced that the Justice Department will not proceed with a $1.8 billion compensation fund following pushback from top Republican lawmakers. The decision represents a significant reversal for the Trump administration.

GOP members had voiced strong opposition to the fund, prompting the administration to abandon the initiative in the face of resistance from within its own party.

cards.headline: British Police Under Investigation for Handcuffing Dying Student
cards.teaser: Authorities are investigating officers who handcuffed Henry Nowak while he was dying, in a case that has drawn widespread attention.
cards.body:
British authorities opened an investigation into police officers who handcuffed a student, Henry Nowak, while he was dying. The case has become increasingly politicized as it has fueled public outrage across the United Kingdom.

Nowak's death and the circumstances surrounding his treatment by police have sparked widespread criticism of law enforcement practices. The investigation will examine the actions of the officers involved and whether proper procedures were followed during the encounter that led to Nowak's death.

cards.headline: Missing New Jersey Congressman Wins Primary After Trump Endorsement
cards.teaser: Republican lawmaker Tom Kean Jr won his primary election despite not being seen in Washington or his district for several months.
cards.body:
Republican Congressman Tom Kean Jr won his primary election after receiving an endorsement from former President Trump. The lawmaker has not been seen in Washington or his New Jersey district for several months.

Despite his prolonged absence from public view, voters selected him as their nominee for the general election.

cards.headline: Protests Intensify in Albania Over Development Linked to Kushner
cards.teaser: Plans for luxury resorts on the Adriatic Sea have sparked growing demonstrations against the Albanian government.
cards.body:
Protests in Albania have grown over plans for luxury resort developments on the Adriatic Sea that involve a project linked to Jared Kushner. The developments have long worried environmentalists concerned about the impact on coastal ecosystems.

The resort plans have become a flashpoint for broader frustrations with the Albanian government. Demonstrators have cited both environmental concerns about the Adriatic coastline and wider grievances about government policies and transparency.

cards.headline: Bear Attacks Worker at Japanese Steel Plant
cards.teaser: A man was attacked by a bear at a steel works facility in Japan.
cards.body:
A bear attacked multiple people at a steel works facility in Japan on Tuesday, injuring four individuals. The incident was captured on video. The bear remained loose within the factory compound following the attack.

Bear encounters in populated and industrial areas have become more frequent in parts of Japan as wildlife ranges expand and overlap with human activity. The attack at the steel manufacturing plant represents an unusual location for such wildlife incidents.

Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche announced that the Justice Department will not proceed with a $1.8 billion compensation fund following pushback from top Republican lawmakers. The decision represents a significant reversal for the Trump administration.

cards.headline: Trump-backed candidate loses Iowa governor primary to MAHA opponent
cards.teaser: Randy Feenstra conceded the Republican primary to Zach Lahn in an upset result.
cards.body:
Randy Feenstra, endorsed by former President Trump, conceded defeat in the Iowa Republican primary for governor. Zach Lahn, who had backing from the MAHA movement, won the contest and will face Democrat Rob Sand in the general election.

The result marked an upset in Iowa politics, as Lahn defeated Trump's preferred candidate in a race to replace retiring Governor Kim Reynolds. The primary victory sets up a competitive November matchup in a state where Democrats believe they can challenge Republican dominance across multiple races.

cards.headline: Los Angeles mayor primary narrows to Bass, Pratt, and Raman
cards.teaser: Karen Bass leads in early returns with Spencer Pratt in second place as votes are counted.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass faces challenges from reality TV star Spencer Pratt and former ally Nithya Raman in the city's mayoral primary. Early election returns show Bass leading with Pratt holding second place as votes continue to be counted.

The race will determine which candidates advance to the general election. Bass, the incumbent mayor, is competing against Pratt, known for his television career, and Raman, a former political ally. Results are still coming in as election officials process ballots from across Los Angeles.

cards.headline: Missing New Jersey congressman wins primary despite months-long absence
cards.teaser: Tom Kean Jr received Trump's endorsement and won his primary despite not being seen since March.
cards.body:
Republican Representative Tom Kean Jr won his New Jersey primary election despite being absent from public view for several months. He had not been seen in Washington or his district since March. Kean received an endorsement from former President Trump ahead of the primary vote.

Kean will face Democrat Rebecca Bennett in the general election after she won her party's primary. Kean said he plans to return to work in person within weeks following his extended absence.

cards.headline: Supreme Court reinstates Republican-favored Alabama congressional map
cards.teaser: Alabama's midterm elections will use districts with six Republican-leaning seats and one Democratic seat.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court reinstated Alabama's congressional district map in a 6-3 decision, allowing the state to use the redrawn boundaries for its 2026 midterm elections. The ruling represents a significant victory for Republicans and comes after an extended legal battle over the map's design.

The reinstated map eliminates one of Alabama's two majority-Black districts, reducing the state to one majority-Black congressional district alongside six Republican-leaning districts. The decision is part of a broader pattern of recent Supreme Court rulings that have limited protections for Black voters under the Voting Rights Act.

cards.headline: Senate Democrats meet with Maine candidate amid texting scandal
cards.teaser: Graham Platner held discussions with Democratic senators despite reports of sexually explicit messages.
cards.body:
Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner met with key Democratic leaders in Washington DC following reports of sexually explicit text messages exchanged with women outside his marriage. The meetings took place as Platner faces renewed scrutiny over the revelations.

Despite the scandal, Democratic leaders appeared to maintain their support for Platner's campaign. The candidate is challenging Senator Susan Collins and represents a central part of Democrats' strategy to regain congressional control, even as he contends with multiple controversies that have threatened his campaign.

cards.headline: Primary elections conclude in six states
cards.teaser: Polls closed across California, Iowa, New Jersey and three other states as midterm matchups take shape.
cards.body:
Voting concluded in six states—California, Iowa, New Jersey, South Dakota, New Mexico, and Montana—as Democrats and Republicans selected their nominees for the midterm elections. The primaries established key matchups across the country, with both parties positioning themselves for the general election.

In Iowa, Democrat Josh Turek won the primary to face Trump-backed Ashley Hinson in a bid to flip the red Senate seat. California's primary determined candidates for governor, the Los Angeles mayoral race, and congressional seats, with Democrats defending key positions and seeking gains in competitive districts.

hero.headline: SpaceX Sets IPO Price at $135 Per Share, Targeting $75 Billion Raise
hero.body:
SpaceX plans to set its initial public offering price at $135 per share, targeting a raise of $75 billion, according to Reuters. The offering would represent one of the largest public market debuts in recent years for a private space company.

The IPO price target comes as SpaceX seeks to capitalize on growing investor interest in commercial space ventures. The company has built its business around satellite launches, astronaut transportation to the International Space Station, and its Starlink satellite internet service. SpaceX has conducted numerous successful missions for NASA and private clients over the past several years.

Morningstar valued SpaceX at $780 billion, significantly less than the valuation implied by the IPO target. This gap between the analyst valuation and the company's pricing reflects differing views on SpaceX's growth prospects and market position. Investment analysts have debated whether the company's ambitious valuation can be justified by its current revenue streams and future projects.

The IPO could substantially increase founder Elon Musk's net worth, according to financial analysts who have suggested it could push his wealth past $1 trillion. Musk has maintained significant ownership of SpaceX while also leading Tesla and pursuing other ventures. The public offering would provide liquidity to early investors and employees who have held equity in the private company for years.

SpaceX has not publicly commented on the IPO timeline or final pricing. The company will need to file detailed financial disclosures with securities regulators before proceeding with a public offering. Market conditions and investor appetite for technology stocks will likely influence the final terms and timing of any deal.

The timing of SpaceX's IPO plans comes amid broader activity in the private technology sector. Other high-profile companies are also pursuing major funding rounds and valuation increases. As investors continue to show strong interest in space technology and related industries, SpaceX's public market debut represents a significant milestone for the commercial space sector.

The space industry has evolved considerably over the past decade, with private companies taking on increasingly important roles in satellite deployment and human spaceflight. SpaceX's business model, which combines government contracts with commercial services, has positioned the company as a leader in this expanding market. The company's Starlink service, which aims to provide global satellite internet coverage, represents a major growth opportunity that investors will likely scrutinize during the IPO process.

The success of SpaceX's public offering could influence investor appetite for other space technology companies and set benchmarks for valuations in the sector. Analysts will be watching to see whether the final IPO pricing aligns with the $135 per share target and how the market responds to the company's long-term growth plans.

cards.teaser: New York and six other states filed suit challenging a payment to TotalEnergies to cancel a wind farm project.
cards.body:
Seven states sued the Trump administration over a nearly $1 billion deal to halt an offshore wind farm project. The administration paid French company TotalEnergies to cancel plans to build offshore wind farms, according to reports from multiple news outlets.

New York led the lawsuit, with officials characterizing the agreement as a fabricated deal designed to block renewable energy development. The states argue the payment represents an improper use of federal funds to prevent clean energy projects from moving forward. The lawsuit seeks to block the deal and recover the funds paid to the company.

cards.headline: MSC Ship Struck by Two Projectiles in Iraqi Port
cards.teaser: A vessel owned by Mediterranean Shipping Company was attacked, highlighting threats to maritime traffic.
cards.body:
A Mediterranean Shipping Company vessel came under attack in an Iraqi port after being struck by two projectiles. The incident highlights the continuing security challenges facing commercial shipping in the region.

The attack occurred amid ongoing U.S.-Iran negotiations aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping route for global oil transport and international commerce. The incident demonstrates that maritime threats persist even as diplomatic efforts work to reduce regional tensions.

cards.headline: CBS News Fires Scott Pelley of 60 Minutes
cards.teaser: The former CBS Evening News anchor was removed following months of tensions with network leadership.
cards.body:
CBS News fired Scott Pelley from 60 Minutes as part of a broader overhaul of the show. The network also dismissed the show's executive producer, executive editor, and correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega.

Pelley publicly objected to the dismissals during a staff meeting, directly criticizing Bari Weiss, CBS News's editor-in-chief. The veteran correspondent, who previously anchored CBS Evening News, attacked the network's management decisions regarding the personnel changes at the long-running investigative program.

cards.headline: Palo Alto Networks Revenue Rises as Customers Increase Cyber Defenses
cards.teaser: The cybersecurity company reported earnings growth driven by demand for AI-enhanced security tools.
cards.body:
Palo Alto Networks reported revenue increases as customers expanded their cybersecurity investments. The company's earnings beat analyst expectations, with artificial intelligence products contributing to growth. The stock jumped following the earnings announcement.

The results addressed skepticism about whether AI would boost cybersecurity demand. Analysts at Jefferies maintained a positive outlook on the company following the earnings report. Palo Alto Networks' valuation reached $243 billion after the stock doubled over a two-month period leading up to the earnings release.

cards.headline: Colorado Enacts Law Tightening Scrutiny of Uber and Lyft
cards.teaser: The legislation increases regulatory oversight following reports of undisclosed sexual assault incidents.
cards.body:
Colorado passed legislation to increase oversight of ride-hailing platforms Uber and Lyft. The law was prompted by a New York Times investigation revealing that Uber had received significantly more reports of sexual assault and sexual misconduct than it had publicly acknowledged.

The new law imposes additional regulatory requirements on ride-hailing companies operating in the state. Colorado lawmakers determined that existing oversight mechanisms were inadequate to protect riders and considered this measure among the stricter state-level responses to ride-hailing safety concerns.

cards.headline: Japan's Nikkei Hits Record High Amid Middle East Concerns
cards.teaser: Asian markets rose despite ongoing tensions in the Middle East affecting global trade.
cards.body:
Japan's Nikkei stock index reached a record high as Asian markets broadly gained. The rally occurred despite continuing concerns about Middle East tensions and their potential impact on global commerce and energy supplies.

The record for the Nikkei came as investors weighed regional economic data against geopolitical risks. Asian markets have shown resilience even as conflicts in the Middle East create uncertainty for shipping routes and energy prices. The gains reflect investor confidence in corporate earnings and regional economic growth despite external pressures.

hero.headline: Microsoft launches Scout, an AI assistant designed to work continuously alongside users
hero.body:
Microsoft announced Scout, a new AI assistant aimed at office workers that operates continuously rather than responding only to specific prompts. Internal documents reviewed by 404 Media show the company wants to make people addicted to the product, which Microsoft is positioning as a personal agent rather than a traditional chatbot.

The assistant was introduced at Microsoft Build, the company's annual developer conference. Unlike conventional AI tools that require users to initiate each interaction, Scout runs persistently in the background and proactively assists with tasks throughout the workday. Microsoft has described Scout as an always-on personal agent that functions like an executive assistant.

The product represents a shift in how Microsoft is approaching AI integration in workplace tools. Rather than limiting AI to discrete tasks or queries, the company is building systems that monitor ongoing work and offer continuous support. This approach mirrors Microsoft's broader strategy of embedding AI capabilities across its product line, though Scout appears designed specifically for sustained engagement.

The revelation about Microsoft's internal goal to create addictive software raises questions about how companies balance user engagement with responsible product design. Documents obtained by 404 Media indicate that making users dependent on Scout is an explicit objective, though Microsoft has publicly framed the product in terms of productivity and convenience. The company has been investing heavily in AI development, including partnerships with OpenAI and efforts to reduce reliance on third-party AI models.

Microsoft also announced other AI-related products at the Build conference, including new AI models intended to lower costs for developers and reduce dependence on OpenAI technology. The company introduced Work IQ APIs and unveiled Project Solara, an Android-based operating system designed around AI agents rather than traditional apps. These announcements suggest Microsoft is pursuing a comprehensive strategy to position AI assistance as central to both personal and enterprise computing.

cards.headline: Microsoft unveils Project Solara, an Android OS built for AI agents
cards.teaser: Microsoft introduced an Android-based operating system designed around AI agents rather than traditional apps.
cards.body:
Microsoft announced Project Solara, an Android-based operating system that prioritizes AI agents over conventional applications. The platform represents a fundamental rethinking of mobile operating systems, shifting focus from app-based interactions to agent-driven experiences.

The announcement came at Microsoft Build, where the company also introduced other AI initiatives. Microsoft has been working to establish itself in AI-powered computing after missing opportunities in the mobile app ecosystem. Project Solara appears to be an attempt to define the next generation of operating systems before competitors establish dominance in agent-based computing.

cards.headline: Cybersecurity company Cyera nears $300 million funding round at $12 billion valuation
cards.teaser: Cyera is close to completing a major funding round that would value the company at 80 times its annual recurring revenue.
cards.body:
Cybersecurity company Cyera is nearing a $300 million funding round led by Evolution Equity Partners that would value the firm at $12 billion. This valuation represents an 80 times multiple of annual recurring revenue.

The company operates in the data security sector, which has drawn substantial venture capital investment as organizations contend with growing threats to sensitive data. The funding reflects ongoing investor appetite for cybersecurity solutions despite broader market challenges.

cards.headline: Scientists find sterilized soil continues respiration for six years
cards.teaser: Researchers discovered that soil kept producing carbon dioxide for six years after being sterilized.
cards.body:
Scientists observed that sterilized soil continued to respire, releasing carbon dioxide, for six years after all living organisms were removed. The finding challenges assumptions about the biological processes necessary for soil respiration.

The discovery suggests that non-biological chemical processes in soil may play a larger role in carbon cycling than previously understood. Soil respiration is a significant component of the global carbon cycle, and understanding its mechanisms has implications for climate science and agriculture.

cards.headline: Microsoft announces Linux tools and RTX Spark desktop for Windows developers
cards.teaser: Microsoft introduced new development tools including Linux integration and specialized hardware at its Build conference.
cards.body:
Microsoft announced several software updates and one hardware product aimed at developers during its Build conference. The company introduced new Linux tools for Windows developers and unveiled the RTX Spark desktop, a machine designed for development work.

The announcements reflect Microsoft's continued efforts to attract developers to its platform by supporting diverse toolchains and workflows. The addition of Linux tools addresses longstanding requests from developers who work across multiple operating systems. The RTX Spark desktop appears to be positioned as a high-performance option for development tasks that require significant computing power.

cards.headline: Insomniac Games shows new footage of Wolverine game featuring combat and story details
cards.teaser: Developers revealed gameplay footage and discussed design choices including a low-gore option and combat mechanics.
cards.body:
Original Card Text - Unchanged

Insomniac Games presented new footage of its upcoming Wolverine game during a PlayStation State of Play event. Developers discussed the game's combat system, which centers on claw-based fighting, and confirmed that players will have the option to reduce gore levels.

The team detailed how the character can die in gameplay and discussed cameo appearances from other X-Men characters. The game has drawn attention for its violent combat, which developers described as fitting the character. The State of Play presentation also included a trailer for MARVEL Tkon: Fighting Souls.

cards.headline: Male bowerbirds incorporate bright human objects into displays to attract mates
cards.teaser: Researchers documented bowerbirds using manufactured items in their courtship displays.
cards.body:
Male bowerbirds have been observed collecting bright human-made objects to decorate their bowers, the structures they build to attract female mates. Researchers studying the birds found they incorporate colorful manufactured items into their traditional courtship displays.

Scientists described the behavior as an example of how human activity is changing wildlife behavior in unexpected ways. Bowerbirds are known for elaborate courtship rituals that involve building decorated structures, and the incorporation of manufactured materials represents an adaptation to environments altered by human presence.

hero.headline: Drake London Signs Four-Year, $141 Million Extension with Falcons
hero.body:
The Atlanta Falcons and wide receiver Drake London have agreed to a four-year contract extension valued at $141 million, according to London's agent. The deal makes London one of the highest-paid receivers in the NFL and keeps him with the Falcons through the 2030 season.

London was set to enter the final year of his rookie contract after Atlanta selected him eighth overall in the 2022 NFL Draft. The extension comes after four seasons in which he has established himself as a central piece of the Falcons' offensive system. The contract places him among the NFL's elite receivers in terms of average annual value.

The USC product has become Atlanta's primary receiving target since entering the league. His size, route-running skills, and hands have made him a consistent option for the team's quarterbacks. By securing London now, the Falcons ensure continuity in their passing attack and demonstrate a commitment to building their offense around proven young talent.

The timing reflects broader trends across professional football. NFL teams have increasingly invested significant resources in top-tier receiving talent in recent years, with numerous players signing contracts exceeding $100 million. London's extension aligns with these market developments and establishes his standing among the league's most valuable pass-catchers.

The Falcons move provides practical benefits heading into the upcoming season. By finalizing the deal before 2026 training camp begins, Atlanta eliminates potential contract discussions that could distract from on-field preparation. The team can now focus on building chemistry among its offensive weapons without the uncertainty of pending negotiations.

For London, the extension offers financial security while keeping him in Atlanta during a critical period for the franchise. The Falcons continue their efforts to compete in the NFC South, and having their top receiver locked in long-term strengthens their ability to compete consistently.

The wide receiver market has experienced substantial growth as teams recognize the importance of securing elite talent at the position. London's deal reflects his development into a difference-maker for the Falcons and the premium teams are willing to pay for receivers who can consistently move the offense and create scoring opportunities.

With London's future now secured, the Falcons' front office can turn its attention to other roster needs and preparations for the upcoming campaign. The extension represents a significant investment in the young receiver and signals confidence in his ability to remain a cornerstone of Atlanta's offense for years to come.

cards.headline: Red Sox Pitcher Garrett Crochet Diagnosed with Low-Grade Lat Strain
cards.teaser: Boston Red Sox left-hander Garrett Crochet will be shut down from throwing after an MRI revealed a low-grade strain in his left lat muscle.
cards.body:
Garrett Crochet experienced a setback in his recovery from left lat tightness, with imaging confirming a low-grade strain. The Red Sox announced that the pitcher will be shut down from throwing activities as he deals with what the team described as a very minor issue. An MRI revealed the extent of the injury after Crochet reported discomfort.

The diagnosis comes at a time when Crochet was already working his way back from the initial lat tightness. Reports indicated he was not particularly close to returning even before this latest setback. The team has not provided a specific timeline for when the left-hander might resume throwing or return to game action.

cards.headline: AJ Brown Says His Knees Are Healthy After Trade to Patriots
cards.teaser: New England Patriots wide receiver AJ Brown addressed concerns about his health, stating his knees are fine and there is nothing to worry about.
cards.body:
AJ Brown spoke publicly about his physical condition following his trade from the Philadelphia Eagles to the New England Patriots. The receiver dismissed any concerns about his knee health, telling reporters his knees are fine and fans should not worry. His comments come after he departed Eagles OTAs, which drew mixed reactions from the organization.

Brown chose to wear the number one jersey with New England despite receiving permission from former Patriots receiver Julian Edelman to wear number 11. Philadelphia general manager Howie Roseman commented on the compensation the Eagles received in the trade, which included a 2028 first-round pick, saying a pick is a pick. The acquisition positions Brown as a key target for Patriots quarterback Drake Maye.

cards.headline: Blue Jackets Defenseman Zach Werenski Wins Norris Trophy
cards.teaser: Columbus Blue Jackets defenseman Zach Werenski captured the Norris Trophy as the NHL's best defenseman.
cards.body:
Zach Werenski earned the Norris Trophy in voting announced by the NHL. The Columbus defenseman finished ahead of other finalists to claim the award recognizing the league's top defenseman. Buffalo Sabres captain Rasmus Dahlin finished third in the voting.

Detroit Red Wings defenseman Moritz Seider finished behind the Michigan native Werenski in the final tally. Washington Capitals defenseman Jakob Chychrun received zero votes despite leading all NHL defensemen in goals scored during the season. Montreal Canadiens rookie Lane Hutson also received votes, with his placement in the voting drawing attention.

cards.headline: Milan Momcilovic Transfers to Kentucky, Set to Arrive Saturday
cards.teaser: Former Iowa State basketball player Milan Momcilovic committed to Kentucky and is scheduled to arrive on campus Saturday.
cards.body:
Milan Momcilovic, the top-ranked player in the college basketball transfer portal, has committed to Kentucky over Arizona and St. John's. The former Iowa State standout arrives Saturday to join head coach Mark Pope's program.

Momcilovic's decision marks a significant portal acquisition for Kentucky as the program continues building its roster for the upcoming season.

cards.headline: Manchester United Agree $35 Million Deal for Atalanta Midfielder Ederson
cards.teaser: Manchester United reached an agreement with Atalanta for Brazilian midfielder Ederson in a deal worth 35 million pounds.
cards.body:
Manchester United have agreed a £35 million fee with Atalanta for Brazilian midfielder Ederson. The 26-year-old will become manager Michael Carrick's first signing at Old Trafford.

Ederson's move to the Premier League represents a significant midfield investment for United as they continue their summer transfer activity.

cards.headline: Alexander Zverev Advances to French Open Semifinals After Defeating Rafael Jodar
cards.teaser: Alexander Zverev defeated teenage qualifier Rafael Jodar in the French Open quarterfinals to move one step closer to his first Grand Slam title.
cards.body:
Alexander Zverev delivered a comprehensive quarter-final performance to defeat teenager Rafael Jodar at the French Open, keeping his pursuit of an elusive Grand Slam title alive. The victory advances him to the semifinals, where he will face Mensik.

Zverev's win came as other top players also progressed through the quarterfinals. Mirra Andreeva advanced to her second Grand Slam semifinal with a dominant display against Sorana Cirstea, while Marta Kostyuk also secured a place in the last four.

hero.headline: Peabo Bryson, R&B Singer Known for Disney Ballads, Dies at 75
hero.body:
Peabo Bryson, the R&B vocalist whose rich tenor voice brought iconic Disney ballads to life, has died at 75. The Grammy-winning singer earned widespread recognition for his performances of "Beauty and the Beast" and "A Whole New World," which became defining songs for a generation of Disney audiences.

Bryson built a career spanning decades in soul and R&B music, earning the nickname "the Voice of Love" for his romantic ballads. His vocal performances on the Disney soundtracks introduced his work to millions of listeners worldwide and secured his place in popular music history. Both songs earned him Grammy Awards and became standards in the American songbook.

The singer's ability to convey emotion through his vocals made him a natural fit for Disney's animated features during the studio's renaissance period in the early 1990s. His duet with Celine Dion on "Beauty and the Beast" and his collaboration with Regina Belle on "A Whole New World" from Aladdin both topped charts and won Academy Awards for Best Original Song. The latter track also earned Bryson and Belle a Grammy Award for Best Pop Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals.

Beyond his Disney work, Bryson maintained a successful career in R&B and soul music. He released numerous albums and collaborated with other major artists throughout his career. His smooth vocal style and interpretive skills made him a respected figure in the music industry.

Bryson had previously suffered a stroke, according to reports from USA Today. His death marks the loss of one of R&B's most distinctive voices and a performer who helped define the sound of modern Disney animation. His recordings continue to be played at weddings, on radio stations, and in homes around the world.

cards.headline: Scott Pelley Fired by CBS News After Clash With New 60 Minutes Leadership
cards.teaser: CBS News terminated veteran journalist Scott Pelley following a public dispute with new management at 60 Minutes.
cards.body:
CBS News has terminated 60 Minutes veteran Scott Pelley following a heated confrontation with Nick Bilton, the newly appointed executive producer, during a Monday morning staff meeting. The clash occurred as the show undergoes significant leadership changes under Bari Weiss's editorial direction, including the recent firing of executive producer, executive editor, and correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega.

Pelley directly criticized Weiss and the network's management decisions during the meeting. In his statement, Pelley expressed that he no longer recognizes the program following Paramount Skydance's takeover of CBS News, accusing leadership of incompetence and calling the "collapse of values at the top" untenable.

cards.headline: Tina Fey's Netflix Series The Four Seasons Finds Success in Second Season
cards.teaser: The Four Seasons returns with a second season that critics are comparing favorably to Fey's earlier work on 30 Rock.
cards.body:
Tina Fey has found success with The Four Seasons on Netflix, with the second season earning praise from critics. The Guardian reviewed the new season as a brilliant follow-up, comparing it favorably to Fey's acclaimed series 30 Rock. The show has been dominating streaming charts, according to Yahoo reports.

The second season features a romantic cliffhanger involving David Tennant, whose casting was explained by the show's co-creator in an interview with Deadline. Galerie Magazine provided details about the destinations featured in the new season. The series, which also stars Steve Carell, has established itself as a major hit for the streaming platform.

cards.headline: Love Island USA Season 8 Debuts on Peacock With First Five Couples
cards.teaser: The reality dating show returned with host Ariana Madix and a new group of single contestants seeking romance.
cards.body:
Love Island USA Season 8 premiered on Peacock with host Ariana Madix and narrator Iain Stirling. The episode introduced five initial couples as single islanders arrived at the villa seeking romantic connections.

Bombshell entries shook up the villa, disrupting the initial pairings. The new season maintains the show's established format, with contestants living together in a tropical setting while forming relationships throughout the competition.

cards.headline: Tom Holland Credits Zendaya as Support System in Hollywood
cards.teaser: The actor described his co-star and partner as a lifeline while navigating the entertainment industry.
cards.body:
Tom Holland said he could not imagine pursuing his acting career without Zendaya, calling her a lifeline in what he described as the wild world of Hollywood. The actor made the comments while discussing their relationship and professional lives.

Holland also praised Zendaya's work in the television series Euphoria and the film The Odyssey. The two actors have worked together on multiple projects and have been public about their relationship. Holland's comments highlight the personal support system that has helped him manage the demands of a high-profile acting career.

cards.headline: Summer House Reunion Features Confrontation Over West Wilson's Relationship
cards.teaser: The second part of the Season 10 reunion included a dramatic appearance by Wilson's ex-girlfriend via video call.
cards.body:
The second part of the Summer House Season 10 reunion featured a dramatic moment when Ciara Miller facilitated a FaceTime call with West Wilson's ex-girlfriend, Meija. The call included timeline details about Wilson's relationship that led to on-stage confrontations. Lindsay Hubbard directed strong language at Wilson, while Amanda Batula left the stage in tears.

The reunion episode, streaming on Peacock, concluded with a tease about the show's future direction. The confrontations centered on Wilson's relationship history and behavior during the season. Host Andy Cohen presided over the multi-part reunion, which has been marked by heightened tensions among cast members.

hero.headline: Supreme Court reinstates Republican-favored Alabama congressional map
hero.teaser: The Court's decision means Alabama's 2026 midterm elections will use a map with six Republican-leaning districts and one Democratic-leaning district.
hero.body:
The U.S. Supreme Court has allowed Alabama to use a redrawn congressional map that eliminates one of the state's two majority-Black districts, issuing a 6-3 decision that represents a significant victory for Republicans and a setback for Black voters.

The ruling permits Alabama to implement its 2023 map in the upcoming midterm elections. A lower court had previously determined that this map was intentionally drawn to discriminate against Black voters and violated the Voting Rights Act. A three-judge panel had rejected the map and ordered a special master to redraw it, which resulted in two majority-Black districts. The panel also issued an injunction preventing Alabama from using another map until after the 2030 census.

Despite these findings, the Supreme Court's majority lifted the injunction without providing any explanation for its decision. The three liberal justices dissented strongly. Justice Sonia Sotomayor wrote that the court had "unceremoniously discards the District Court's meticulously documented and supported discriminatory-intent finding" without sound basis. She noted that "the record showed that Alabama made an intentional choice to perpetuate and entrench, rather than remedy and uproot, the racial discrimination."

Under the reinstated map, Alabama will have five congressional districts represented by white Republicans and two represented by Black Democrats. Notably, the new map eliminates the seat held by Representative Shomari Figures, which stretched from Mobile through the state's Black Belt, and replaces it with a Republican district.

The Supreme Court's decision comes just days after the same court gutted Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act in a case involving Louisiana's congressional districts. Alabama quickly returned to the Supreme Court following that ruling to request removal of the injunction, which the court granted on Monday.

The decision reflects an aggressive approach by the court's conservative majority in allowing Republican-controlled states to redraw districts that reduce the influence of Black voters. In the past, the Supreme Court has generally refused to overturn election rules on the eve of elections. However, the court has now abandoned this principle in both the Louisiana case, where it issued its decision while voting was underway, and in Alabama.

Republicans in other states have moved quickly to capitalize on this development. Tennessee, Louisiana, and South Carolina have all begun efforts to implement new maps designed to boost Republican electoral chances in the upcoming elections.

The Alabama primary was originally scheduled for May 19, but Republicans passed legislation last week moving the date in anticipation of the Supreme Court's action. The new map will shape how Alabama's voters are grouped and represented in the House of Representatives for the current election cycle.

cards.headline: U.S. and Iranian forces exchange strikes as peace talks stall
cards.teaser: U.S.
cards.body:
U.S. and Iranian forces exchanged strikes Tuesday as peace talks remained stalled and tensions escalated across the Middle East. American aircraft fired on Iranian military sites over the weekend, including Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway through which roughly one-fifth of global petroleum passes.

The U.S. military characterized its response as self-defense against Iranian aggression across the region. The confrontation widened beyond direct exchanges between the two nations, raising concerns about potential broader regional conflict as diplomatic efforts showed no signs of progress.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins Democratic primary for New Mexico governor
cards.teaser: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland secured the Democratic nomination to succeed Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham and could become the first Native American woman elected governor.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary in New Mexico's gubernatorial race, positioning herself to potentially make history as the first Native American woman elected governor of any state. Haaland, who served as Interior Secretary under President Biden, celebrated her victory at a historic plaza in Albuquerque's Old Town neighborhood.

Haaland will face the Republican nominee in November's general election to replace outgoing Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham. Her experience includes service in both Congress and the Biden administration's cabinet, where she oversaw federal land management and Native American affairs.

cards.headline: CBS fires Scott Pelley from '60 Minutes' after confrontation with new producer
cards.teaser: Veteran anchor Scott Pelley was terminated after challenging new executive producer Nick Bilton during a staff meeting on Bilton's first day.
cards.body:
Scott Pelley, a veteran correspondent at '60 Minutes,' was fired by newly appointed executive producer Nick Bilton following a heated staff meeting on Bilton's first day. During the meeting, Pelley criticized CBS News management's decision to remove the show's previous executive producer and executive editor, as well as correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega.

Pelley directly attacked Bari Weiss, CBS News' editor-in-chief, during the confrontation with Bilton and CBS News managing editor Charles Forelle present. The personnel changes represented a broader overhaul of the long-running program, triggering tensions between veteran talent and new leadership at the network.

cards.headline: Iowa sets November matchups for governor and Senate races
cards.teaser: Voters selected nominees for competitive statewide races, with businessman Zach Lahn and State Auditor Rob Sand winning their respective gubernatorial primaries.
cards.body:
Iowa's primary elections have set up two competitive general election races. In the gubernatorial contest, Republican businessman Zach Lahn will face Democrat Rob Sand, the state auditor. Lahn secured the Republican nomination after defeating four challengers, including U.S. Rep. Randy Feenstra. Lahn received backing from Turning Point Action.

For the U.S. Senate race, Democratic state Rep. Josh Turek will compete against Republican U.S. Rep. Ashley Hinson. Both matchups will determine leadership for Iowa as the state remains a battleground in November's general elections.

cards.headline: California holds primaries for governor and Los Angeles mayor
cards.teaser: Voters are selecting nominees in crowded races to replace Gov. Gavin Newsom and determine whether Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass wins reelection.
cards.body:
California voters headed to the polls Tuesday in primary elections for governor, Los Angeles mayor, and congressional seats. The gubernatorial race features Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer, and Xavier Becerra competing alongside Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton to replace Gov. Gavin Newsom. In Los Angeles, incumbent Mayor Karen Bass faces challengers Nithya Raman and Spencer Pratt in a competitive primary.

The primaries will narrow the fields to two candidates in each race. With polls closing at 8pm local time, California's notoriously slow vote-counting system means results from the tightest contests may take days to become clear.

cards.headline: Iowa House race sets up third consecutive matchup between Miller-Meeks and Bohannan
cards.teaser: Republican Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks and Democrat Christina Bohannan will face each other again in Iowa's 1st Congressional District.
